assumptions: Full finite real Hilbert/Borel E including0; W is C1 and exp(-W) is genuinely integrable. mu is exactly the normalized volume.tilted(-W) Gibbs probability, whose density is positive. No curvature or spectral gap is assumed.

Fix SAME original weighted-L2 real partial-linear gradient D with exact compact-C-infinity genuine gradient graph and closability before ALL u in D.closure.domain. Each queried u satisfies D.closure u=0 as an actual vector L2 class, not a pointwise derivative assertion or final kernel certificate.
units.statement: For the SAME original Gibbs compact-gradient closure, EVERY domain element u with D.closure u=0 is weighted-AE ONE real constant. This is only one direction; constant-domain membership and full kernel equality are not asserted.

steps.title: Keep the SAME original closure graph and its actual representatives
steps.text: Apply the accepted ordinary distributional theorem to (u,D.closure u) in the SAME original graph. It derives true local-volume integrability and legal C1 compact directional products/weak identity; no rough differentiability or final kernel characterization is supplied.

steps.title: Transfer the actual zero vector class in the correct direction
steps.text: D.closure u=0 gives its actual AE representative zero under mu. Genuine exp(-W) integrability and strictly positive normalized density imply volume<<mu, so zero also holds volume-AE. The reverse absolute-continuity direction would not justify this step.

steps.title: Derive the legal ordinary zero weak derivative and one constant
steps.text: Use actual integral congruence to turn the left weak-gradient integral into0, retaining the right product integrability. Apply the new ordinary weak-zero-gradient leaf to derive volume-AE ONE constant for this same u.

steps.title: Transfer constancy back to the actual Gibbs law and keep the one-way boundary
steps.text: Since mu<<volume, the very same constant representative is mu-AE. This does not put constants into the original closure domain, identify the full kernel/range, prove centering/residual convergence, Poincare/BL or a paper main result.
